messages:
customer_qa: Hey team — multiple customers reporting intermittent 400s from /v1/embeddings and a correlated billing spike. Error message: "400 Bad Request: embedding dimension mismatch". Ticket #6421. Anyone seen this?
support_prod: Thanks, can you paste a redacted request body + headers (no API keys) and a sample response? Also which model & region?
customer_qa: Example from Node client (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-large-v1",
  "input": [[ [0.12, 0.05, 0.9, ... 1024 values ...] ]]  // client double-wrapped the vector
}
```
Response returned: `400 Bad Request` with body: `{"error":"embedding dimension 1024 != expected 1536"}`
support_prod: Hmm mixing dims. Did they change model or accidentally send openai-style 1536-dim vectors to our 1024 model?
sam_ml: Quick note: our embeddings endpoint expects `input` to be either a single string/vector OR a list of strings/vectors. A common client bug: double-wrapping with an extra array layer (e.g., `[[vec]]` instead of `[vec]`) makes the server try to interpret inner arrays incorrectly and triggers a dimension check failure during validation.
customer_qa: Also saw a variant where the client sent a scalar when we expected a list: `input: 0.12` — leading to a different 400 but same billing behavior because requests still consumed tokens.
deploy-bot: api-gateway: request_id=abc123 status=400 path=/v1/embeddings model=rwd-embed-large-v1
support_prod: Can you share a curl repro we can run? Need exact header pattern.
customer_qa: Repro curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
 -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-large-v1","input":[[[0.12,0.05,0.9,...1024 values...]]]}'
```
sam_ml: Verified locally — double-wrapped array yields schema parse that looks like: shape [1][1][1024] vs expected [1][1024]. Our validator then infers outer dims and runs dimension check producing that error.
support_prod: Short-term mitigation: ask customers to ensure they pass a single-level array for batched vectors or a raw vector for single requests. Node SDKs historically did `Array.isArray` checks that mistakenly wrap.
sam_ml: Long-term fix proposal: server-side stricter validation that detects nested arrays and returns a clear actionable error: "Invalid input shape: found nested arrays; send either a single vector or a flat list of vectors. See docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/format". Also optionally auto-flatten single redundant nesting for best-effort compatibility.
customer_qa: Customer also flagged unexpected charges because many of these malformed calls still counted against usage before failing. Can finance look?
finance_ellie: Escalating — will review ticket #6421 for potential credits. Need request IDs and timestamps; can you attach logs?
support_prod: Attaching request ids from logs in the ticket. Also adding suggested client-side snippet to avoid the bug: 
```js
// ensure single-level batch
function normalizeInput(x){
  if (Array.isArray(x) && Array.isArray(x[0]) && Array.isArray(x[0][0])){
    return x.flat(1); // remove one accidental nesting\  }
  return x;
}
```
sam_ml: Added note: we should update SDK docs and a short migration note in the API changelog. I'll open a PR for server validation by EOD.
support_prod: Customer applied the client fix and error rate dropped to near zero. They still want billing review.
customer_qa: Confirmed with customer: after switching to non-wrapped batched arrays, embeddings succeed and latency normal. Will follow up if anything else. :thumbsup:
finance_ellie: Got the logs, starting billing review. Will update ticket with decision. :eyes:
